transcript.text: Bosch KGN34NL3AG - some days it's fine, other days it just clicks every few minutes at the back and doesn't seem to run, and the freezer starts getting soft. Then it starts working again by itself. What's going on?

That clicking sound followed by silence usually means the compressor is trying to start but failing, often due to a faulty start relay or an overheating motor. Since it sometimes works again, this points to an electrical component like the start relay rather than a complete mechanical seizure of the compressor itself. To narrow this down safely, please check that the plug is fully inserted and the socket has power (try a lamp in it), and also see if the cooling coils at the back or underneath are dusty or pushed tight against the wall.

Thank you. The fridge is plugged directly into the wall socket, and it behaves the same when I try another socket. The back is a bit dusty, but there is a gap between it and the wall. I haven't noticed any burning smell, and nothing has tripped.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Since the power supply is good and there's no burning smell, the intermittent clicking with soft freezer ice points to the start relay (or overload protector) failing to engage the compressor. This part is cheap and common to replace. Please unplug the fridge, remove the rear lower access panel, and check that small plastic box on the compressor for any signs of heat damage or melting. If it looks damaged, that suggests the fault; if it looks fine, we may need an engineer to test the compressor windings.

I'm not sure how to remove the rear lower panel, and I can't say whether the box is heat damaged because I haven't looked at it closely. I can tell you the clicking comes from the box on the side of the compressor at the bottom back. There's no burning smell and nothing has tripped, so do you still want me to stop using the fridge completely? How exactly do I get the panel off?

I cannot give you specific instructions on how to remove the rear panel for this model as I do not have access to the manufacturer's service manual or disassembly diagrams. Attempting to force panels off can damage clips or internal wiring. Given that the clicking is coming from the compressor area and the cooling is intermittent, the most likely cause is a failing start relay or overload protector on the compressor itself. This is an electrical component that requires replacement by a qualified engineer who has the tools to test the compressor windings safely and handle refrigerant systems if needed. I recommend contacting Bosch support or a local appliance repair technician to diagnose and replace this part.
